daily_scan.notes: Breadth-first single-alias pass across all 9 due records (adocia-adoxlong, ascendis-transcon-novo, ascletis-asc30, astrazeneca-zoladex, cspc-syh2082, lilly-eloralintide, owlbio-kyungdong-xtina, samsung-bioepis-g2gbio-gb7001, zealand-petrelintide); the other 36 were checked within the last 1-2 days and are quiet 21+ days, so correctly throttled. 8 of the 9 due records reconfirmed existing findings with no material new information this run. cspc-syh2082 turned up genuine late-discovered news: an FDA clinical-trial clearance (2026-02-16, wire-corroborated) and a clinicaltrials.gov Phase I dose-escalation study (NCT07736404) with an actual dosing start of 2026-04-13 and status Active, not recruiting -- both logged as new findings and stage_label advanced Preclinical -> Phase 1 (both discovered ~5-7 months after the fact, well outside the freshness window, so treated as discovered-late rather than headline). Track B1: 14/14 fixed watchlist rows queried. Code harvest surfaced 11 code-pattern strings across results (ALT-M5, AZD6234, NN1706, DA-3091, AZD8233, MET-233i, HM15275, ABBV-295, GUB014295, PT404, AZD9550); most resolved immediately as already-tracked aliases, parent-molecule identifiers or known decoys. 2 needed a bounded query: AZD6234 (AstraZeneca amylin analog; confirmed weekly-only dosing, decoy, no LAI program) and a claim that Hanmi's HM15275 (an existing once-weekly decoy) is also being developed in patch and once-monthly formulations -- traced to a single Tier 2/3 outlet (medicopharma.co.kr) using aspirational framing with no corroboration and no concrete technical detail, so it does not clear the candidate creation bar and was not queued. ALT-M5 (Alteogen) resolved as a genuine new candidate via the fixed watchlist queries themselves (see below), so no extra bounded query was needed for it. 4 rotation-list rows queried (abbv-295, pt404, lilly-camurus, alteogen-monthly), resuming after ct-g32 and wrapping to the start of the list; abbv-295/pt404/lilly-camurus reconfirmed existing watchlist documentation with nothing new. alteogen-monthly is now resolved: Alteogen announced (2026-09-17, two independent Tier 2 outlets) a PCT filing for a new 'Long-Acting Conjugate' platform and a once-monthly obesity candidate ALT-M5 with animal data on monthly dosing and rebound suppression -- logged as new candidate cand-2026-09-18-001 (near_bar, missing only second_dated_event); PROPOSING this row be retired from the rotation list now that it has a candidate entry. B3 cheap pass (2/2 searches spent): re-checked cand-2026-09-17-001 (Samik Pharmaceutical) -- found only the same patent registration with a more precise date (Aug 27, 2026), not a new dated event, remains pending/near_bar; re-checked cand-2026-09-13-001 (Prolynx) -- still no IND/trial registration since the Dec 2025 Series A, remains pending/near_bar. Stall rule checked across all 16 unresolved candidates -- oldest is 16 days old, none 30+ days, none triggered. No new EGRESS_BLOCKED domains this run (no direct WebFetch attempted; all sources reached via search). clinicaltrials.gov and patents.google.com both reached via search again this run (e.g. NCT07736404, NCT07484204).

weekly_sweep.notes: Track B2 structural sweep across all 6 categories (conference abstract indices, KIPRIS/USPTO/WIPO patent filings, KOSDAQ tech-listing pipeline, clinicaltrials.gov new-registration feed by mechanism/title, university tech-transfer, VC/deal databases), ~30 queries. Conference indices and the KOSDAQ pipeline were quiet as expected for September (off-season). Two existing-umbrella items the sweep turned up (a G2GBio semaglutide-patent priority-date item, and Mapi Pharma's NCT07563699 registration) were checked against the actual umbrella files and found already logged from a prior run -- not re-added, avoiding a duplicate finding. One new candidate cleared the creation bar and was queued: cand-2026-09-13-001 Prolynx ($70M Series A, tunable-release linker + microsphere-hydrogel depot platform targeting monthly/quarterly incretin dosing, corroborated by two independent Tier 2 outlets). A second lead (Persist AI, an AI/robotics formulation-screening vendor rather than a drug developer) did not clear the bar on sourcing/specificity and was left out rather than logged as a thin candidate. Track B3 weekly deep pass covered all 16 previously-unresolved candidates (one query each, see coverage.candidate_follow_up) -- five escalated to ready_for_promotion on their own previously-logged evidence (each already had a Tier-1 stage-bearing event, e.g. a clinicaltrials.gov trial registration, which alone clears the promotion bar): cand-2026-09-02-005 (Bostal/B2227), cand-2026-09-02-006 (Anxo/AX251), cand-2026-09-02-008 (BioCorRx/BICX104), cand-2026-09-02-009 (Zhuhai Huahaikang/HHK001), cand-2026-09-09-002 (GSK/felcorekibart -- flagged with a standing scope caveat, systemic respiratory mAb not a depot/LAI asset). One re-fuzzy-match caught a registry-growth case per the skill's own worked example: cand-2026-09-02-007 (CSPC ZhongQi/SYHX2008) now scores 0.58 against the newly-promoted cspc-syh2082 (same CSPC Pharmaceutical Group parent, different asset) -- flagged as a merge case rather than escalated, per the mechanical >=0.55 rule.
